expressivity_note: One cat map expresses at least N^2/T(N) ~ O(N) distinct orbits (sampled: 123/245/487 for N=64/128/256), and every orbit is a LINEAR periodic function (A^t x_0).  N independent blocks express N UNCONSTRAINED functions.  The parameter saving of one map (4 params vs N blocks) is exactly RNN weight-sharing — standard, not chaotic — and it buys only linear periodic routes, far below what N blocks can express.

chaotic_router.construction: encoder training (same as any learned router)
chaotic_router.index: orbit tables: O(N^2/T * T) = O(N^2) cells (~170 orbits x ~96 cells)
chaotic_router.inference: orbit scan: O(orbit_len) ~ 82.1 steps; expected with reachability p=0.77: ~107 steps (retries)
chaotic_router.reachability_limit: single-cell target reachable only 0.0045 of the time

hash_table.note: context->expert is exactly what the chaotic encoder must learn ANYWAY; the hash does it directly without the orbit scan.

moe_router.inference: O(K) softmax (or O(log K) with tree)
moe_router.note: same training cost as the chaotic encoder, no scan, no reachability limit.

C_total.chaotic: C_train(encoder) + C_index(O(N^2)) + C_infer(O(orbit)) + C_corr(0) = WORSE than hash on index AND inference, equal on training
C_total.verdict: The chaotic router must train the same encoder as any router, then ADDS an O(N^2) index and an O(orbit) scan, and is limited by reachability.  It is a strictly more expensive hash. (TZ 18.1, 18.2: any win vanishes after preprocessing; chaotic routing == lookup with extra cost.)

hidden_transfer_note: The only 'cheap' part of chaos — the closed form A^t (exp01) — has zero construction cost, but it matches (not beats) the honest baseline (matrix power O(log t)).  The O(t) comparison is a strawman.  Everything else (routing) shifts cost INTO index/training, exactly the hidden transfer the TZ warns about.
